plan.title: Liver 3-group DESeq2 LRT + per-treatment contrasts
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, Homo sapiens, liver) in one batch, with three groups of four replicates each: control, treated_a, treated_b. The question has two parts, in order: which genes differ across the three groups at all (an omnibus test, since condition spans k-1 = 2 coefficients and no single Wald coefficient answers it), and which genes each treatment changes relative to control (two named contrasts). The plan therefore (1) runs sample-structure QC first — blind vst, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap — to confirm grouping and detect outliers before any test; (2) fits DESeq2 with median-of-ratios size factors, a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples), then the LRT (full ~condition vs reduced ~1) for the any-difference question, followed by two pairwise Wald contrasts against the explicit reference level control, with ashr-shrunken log2 fold changes (ashr because a contrast against the reference with three levels is still reported alongside coefficient-based results and ashr handles contrasts generally), BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 within each contrast with independent filtering on; (3) re-runs the same question with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as a second method, since with 4 replicates per group the two tools call some genes the other does not; (4) reports per-contrast gene tables (unshrunken and shrunken LFC plus lfcSE, ranked on the shrunken value), MA and dispersion diagnostics, the p-value histogram, and the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set. One caveat shapes the plan: the counts come from Salmon as a gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so whether the length correction occurred is not established. The model is fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and the report must state that the offset is lost (a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression); no tximport run and no invented length input.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
